title: The Evening Brief: Whales Push Record $1.6B Onto Exchanges This Week
dek: Bitcoin held near $80,318 as the desk's Whale Watch board recorded the largest weekly inflow onto exchanges in its recent record, even as spot Bitcoin ETFs took in money over the week.
author: GoCheckMyCrypto
key_fact: The Whale Watch board shows $1,591 million moving onto exchanges in the week ending October 25, the largest weekly figure in the board's recent record, a sign of caution that sits alongside a calm Fear & Greed reading of 54.
bottom_line: The desk's Whale Watch board recorded $1,591 million moving onto exchanges in the week ending October 25, the largest weekly figure in its recent record, while spot Bitcoin ETFs took in $301.2M over the week through October 23 despite a $137.9M outflow on the day itself. Bitcoin held near $80,318, down 0.29% over 24 hours and down 4.23% over thirty days, with funding and the Fear & Greed Index at 54 both reading calm rather than stressed. No story published today explains the driver behind the exchange inflows, and the desk's regulatory threads carry no near-term dated checkpoint. The coming days will show whether this week's exchange-bound flow continues or reverses as it did the week ending October 18.
body: Bitcoin traded at $80,318 on the desk's board Sunday, little changed on a quiet day with no new stories published. The single thread in the data is a split between what short-term traders are doing with their coins and what the broader sentiment and ETF readings say: exchange flows point toward caution while funding, fear/greed, and the week's ETF tally stay closer to neutral or positive.

The desk's Whale Watch board shows $255,471,774 moving onto exchanges over the past 72 hours, with bitcoin accounting for $163,814,601 of that net and ether accounting for $91,657,173. The board's biggest single moves include $155,650,858 in bitcoin and $91,657,173 in ether both flowing to Coinbase Institutional, alongside $124,544,615 in USDT moving to Bitfinex. Zooming out to the board's weekly record, the week ending October 25 shows $1,591 million moving onto exchanges, the largest figure among the four weeks on the board, surpassing the week ending October 11 ($1,503 million onto exchanges), the week ending October 4 ($804 million onto exchanges), and reversing the week ending October 18, when $205 million moved off exchanges.

On the price side, Bitcoin is down 0.29% over 24 hours, down 0.73% over seven days, and down 4.23% over thirty days. Ether is down 0.33% over 24 hours, down 1.82% over seven days, and down 12.30% over thirty days. Solana is down 0.09% over 24 hours, down 1.06% over seven days, and down 12.60% over thirty days. XRP is up 0.45% over 24 hours and up 0.44% over seven days, though it remains down 15.36% over thirty days. BNB is up 0.55% over 24 hours and up 3.01% over seven days, down 4.82% over thirty days. Among the largest coins, the day's gainers were QNT, up 7.96% over 24 hours, ENA, up 7.22%, and PYTH, up 7.14%, while XDC, PEPE, and XMR led losers, down 4.88%, 4.27%, and 3.08% respectively over 24 hours.

The reporting does not name a specific driver for this week's exchange inflows; no story published today addresses the cause. What the boards show is a divergence: spot Bitcoin ETFs saw net outflows of $137.9M on the day, October 23, but took in $301.2M over the week through October 23, a week of net buying even as the whale data shows coins moving toward exchanges. The desk's Fear & Greed Index reads 54, labeled Neutral, within its recent 30-day range of 50 to 74, which does not suggest acute stress despite the exchange-flow pattern.

The desk's leverage board shows funding staying calm across majors. Bitcoin funding on OKX runs at 0.0081% per eight hours, annualized to 8.8%, with a long/short ratio of 2.15 and liquidations over a 6-hour window totaling $470,193 in longs against $25,548 in shorts. Ether funding sits lower, at 0.0039% per eight hours annualized to 4.3%, with $1,526,514 in long liquidations against $480,305 in short liquidations over a 2-hour window, a short but sharper burst than bitcoin's. Solana's long/short ratio runs highest among majors at 2.97, with liquidations skewed toward shorts, $604,809 against $413,498 in longs over 14 hours. None of these figures signal the kind of forced unwind that would explain the week's exchange inflows on their own.

No regulatory story published today, and the desk's regulatory_watch record shows no checkpoint dated for the days immediately ahead; the live threads the desk has covered, including the CLARITY Act, the EU's Markets in Crypto-Assets framework, and the US executive order track, carry only dates already passed or dates not yet stated in the desk's own reporting. What to watch in the coming days is whether the exchange-inflow pattern on the Whale Watch board continues or reverses, as it did in the week ending October 18, and whether the ETF tally's weekly inflow holds against the latest daily outflow once the next session prints.
